title: Your brain lies to you at 3am
points: Overthinking at night isn't wisdom - it's just your prefrontal cortex going offline.
Your brain replays old arguments because unresolved threat feels unfinished.
The fix isn't 'stop thinking.' It's giving the thought a scheduled time tomorrow.
Write it down. Your brain stops guarding a thought once it's externalized.

title: 8 Psychological Reasons You Self-Sabotage

scenes.narration: Self-sabotage rarely feels like sabotage while it's happening. It feels like a good reason to quit right before something works.
Reason one: familiarity feels safer than success. If you've never had it, your brain treats it as a threat, not a reward.
Reason two: a fear of exceeding what your family or friends have achieved. Psychologists call this a loyalty bind.
Reason three: perfectionism disguised as procrastination. You delay starting so the unfinished version can never be judged.
Reason four: low self-worth needs the story confirmed. Winning would contradict the identity you've built your whole life around.
Reason five: control. Quitting on your own terms feels safer than being rejected on someone else's.
Reason six: your nervous system confuses growth with danger. Any spike in visibility can trigger a full anxiety response.
Reason seven: unprocessed past failure. One bad result years ago quietly wrote a rule your brain still follows today.
Reason eight: nobody ever taught you what safety feels like when things go right. So your body reroutes it back to what's familiar.
None of these mean something is wrong with you. They mean your brain is doing exactly what it was trained to do - and it can be retrained.
